My thoughts on this are best described as a process flow.

 

Did the Target of Wrest the Mind deal damage?

Just a quick clarification on my point in regard to ‘skipping to the end and back to the middle.’ While that does appear to be what I’m saying, it’s not. What I’m saying is that the card has two triggers, one in the middle and one on the bottom. The trigger in the middle only applies the actions listed in the middle; it does not continue to the bottom. Rather, the middle trigger generates some actions, and those actions can fire other triggers, and itself as a card can be one of those triggers, in which case the same card at a different place can be in two parts of the stack at the same time. Argent Adepts instruments and songs are a perfect example of this.
As an example of what I’m explaining, using Wrest the Mind and two made up targets named X and Y, assume Wrest the Mind is played on X. X has the effect that the first time per turn it’s dealt damage by a target, it deals damage to that target, and Y has a similar effect, except it then deals damage to one other target. X attempts to deal damage (for some reason). Wrest the Mind triggers on this (first time). Visionary redirects this to Y. Y then reacts by redirecting that damage back to it’s source (X). X now reacts by attempting to deal damage back to the source (Y), but it triggers Wrest the Mind, and redirects to another unknown (in this story) target. Now, the stack is X deal damage (interrupted), Wrest the Mind redirects damage (first time), Y retaliates to damage, X retaliates to damage (interrupted), Wrest the Mind redirects damage (second time). X does not retaliate again, as I tried to word it in such a way as one retaliation per turn rather than one retaliation per turn per target, to keep it as simple as possible. Since no other triggers react, execution continues with the second triggering of Wrest the Mind, with X attack finishing, then Visionary dealing X and herself damage (assuming no triggers). With that finished, X is already finished with damage. Y now deals another target damage. Now that Y is finished, it goes back to Wrest the Mind again, which has Visionary dealing damage to X and herself.
The issue isn’t Wrest the Mind bouncing around (technically, it’s being inserted into the stack a second time at a different execution point, the original execution point of the card at the first insertion point is currently paused in place). The issue is whether a card can react to the destruction of the target before Visionary deals herself damage. That is all I have to say on this topic.

One thing I will say, when Christopher said the game had no concept of a stack, he went on to explain a queue. Then when he explained how the game actually works, he explained a stack system. Though I could easily see someone using the word ‘stack’ to assume any kind of ordered listing.
Basically, if a game is queue based, when resolving a card, nothing else will happen until the card is finished. If anything were to trigger, the reaction is placed into a queue and does not have any of its actions resolved. Once the initial card is finished, the first action put into the queue is resolved. If there are any triggers activated for that card, they are added to the end of the queue of whatever else had been added. It’s a case of whichever reaction has been waiting the longest (no matter what triggered it) is the first action to take effect. (Christopher said this game is not this).
In a stack based game, when a card is resolving, if something triggers, the current card goes to top of the stack, and the reaction to the trigger resolves. If that reaction triggers other reactions, the current reaction goes to the top of the stack at its current instruction and the new reaction interrupts. When a reaction finally finishes, the top of the stack resumes at the instruction it left off. This is basically Christopher explained the game (without using the term ‘stack’ of course).
I thought I would provide this information just in case anyone was confused between the idea of a queue based game and a stack based game.
